newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban capture district in northwest.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban capture district in northwest.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamist Taleban militia captured a small district northwest of Kabul on Friday after three days of fighting with opposition forces, an Afghan news service said.

The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said the Taleban seized Chardihi district in the Ghorband Valley, about 75 km (47 miles) from the Afghan capital, from the Shi'ite Moslem militia backed by ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood and northern General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
It said four Taleban had been killed and seven wounded in the battle. Six opposition fighters were killed and 12 wounded.

In the past two weeks, the Taleban have made a rapid push into the foothills of the Hindu Kush, some 100 km (60 miles) north of Kabul, re-occupying positions they held in October shortly after taking the capital.
The Taleban, who have taken control of about two-thirds of Afghanistan, are committed to bringing their strict version of Islam's Shariah law to the country.
